# Input, actions and Unicode text

API entries:

- [`up.input.Input`](#input-Input)
- [`up.input.Key`](#input-Key)
- [`up.input.Pointer`](#input-Pointer)
- [`up.input.Gamepad`](#input-Gamepad)
- [`up.input.Action`](#input-Action)
- [`up.input.ActionBinding`](#input-ActionBinding)
- [`up.input.ActionMap`](#input-ActionMap)


[Task index](core.md) · [GameContext](lifecycle.md#core-GameContext) · [Replay](testing.md)

Read ctx.input during fixed update. Use held state for movement and pressed/
released edges for one-shot actions. Normalized Key has ten defaults; use
Input.PhysicalKey for distinct Q/E/1/2 controls. Input setters are host/test
builders; an ordinary game reads the host's snapshot instead of polling SDL
or DOM directly. Snapshot/extension storage is inline; copying it owns the
copy, while event/text slices borrow the current input storage.

In ActionMap signatures, `Map` means [`up.input.ActionMap`](#input-ActionMap),
`Binding` means [`up.input.ActionBinding`](#input-ActionBinding), and
`input.Input` means [`up.input.Input`](#input-Input). In extension signatures,
`State` means `up.input.Input.Extended` and `Event` means
`up.input.Input.InputEvent`; both are nested public aliases shown below.

## Rebinding recipe

ActionMap.init owns its action/cache allocations and needs deinit. It copies
definitions but borrows their name/context strings; keep those strings alive.
The borrowed `ActionMap{ .actions = &definitions }` form supports value
queries but rejects mutation with `ImmutableActionMap`. Owned maps update
their cached edges once each fixed tick, after rebinding.

[Compiled source](../../examples/api_reference_recipes.zig#L51) (`rebind`):

```zig
pub fn rebind(allocator: std.mem.Allocator) !void {
    const definitions = [_]up.input.Action{
        .{ .name = "interact", .binding = .{ .physical_key = .q } },
    };
    var actions = try up.input.ActionMap.init(allocator, &definitions);
    defer actions.deinit();
    try actions.rebind("game", "interact", .{ .physical_key = .r });
    var input = up.input.Input{};
    input.setPhysical(.r, true, false); // A host observation, supplied by this test.
    actions.update(input);
    if (!actions.wasPressed("game", "interact")) return error.RebindDidNotTakeEffect;
}
```


The sample supplies a test key observation. In a game replace that observation
with `actions.update(ctx.input.*)`. Rebinding unknown actions/bindings is an
error. In-memory rebinding is portable; native save/load/attachAppData helpers
need a filesystem. Browser games should save chosen bindings as game-owned
bytes through [SaveStore](audio-save.md#core-SaveStore).

## Text and composition

Request `try ctx.setTextInput(true)` when a name field opens and false when
it closes. This requests host activation; it does not fabricate input.
`ctx.input.extended.active` reports observed activation. Consume ordered
`eventSlice()` events and use `eventText(event)` for their UTF-8 bytes. Copy
commits into game-owned storage; render composition_update preedit separately.
The [minimal game](lifecycle.md) shows bounded commit copying; the
[compiled input workbench](../../examples/input_workbench_game.zig) also handles
preedit, rebinding and backspace.

Events/text are bounded to 32 events and 1024 text bytes per snapshot. Overflow
is observable through extended.overflow; do not assume arbitrary pastes fit.
Headless builders can report `InputOverflow`, `InvalidUtf8` or
`TextInputInactive`; context activation can report `TextInputUnavailable`.
Edges/events occur once on the first consuming update; clear transients before
supplying another catch-up tick yourself. The [input guide](../guides/input.md)
and [compatibility contract](../guides/input-v2-compatibility.md) define IME,
selection units, focus loss, buffering and UPR5 encoding.

<a id="input-Input-Snapshot"></a>
### `up.input.Input.Snapshot`

[Source declaration](../../src/input.zig#L86).

A complete, normalized view of game-facing input for one simulation tick.

Runtime hosts apply one snapshot before every fixed update. A snapshot
preserves held state and latched edges independently, because a press
and release may both occur between simulation ticks.

[`fromInput`](#input-Input-Snapshot-fromInput) · [`apply`](#input-Input-Snapshot-apply) · [`clearTransient`](#input-Input-Snapshot-clearTransient) · [`merge`](#input-Input-Snapshot-merge) · [`isFinite`](#input-Input-Snapshot-isFinite)
